concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: The original DPA requires notification no later than 48 hours after awareness of a breach. The amendment replacing this provision takes effect on 1 October 2026, after 15 September 2026.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment replaced the breach notification deadline with no later than 24 hours after awareness, effective 1 October 2026 and still in force on 1 November 2026.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment reduced the on-site audit prior written notice period from 30 days to 20 days, effective 1 October 2026.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amended liability clause caps the Processor's aggregate liability for breaches of the DPA at EUR 1,000,000, replacing the earlier fee-based formula.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: The amended liability clause expressly states that the EUR 1,000,000 cap does not apply to breaches of the confidentiality section.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd is listed as an approved Sub-processor in the DPA annex, and its withdrawal only takes effect on 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: The approval of Meridian Mail Ltd was withdrawn effective 1 January 2027, and the later emergency permission is limited to a specific incident and interval in May 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, personal data is stored or processed in Norway, Estonia, Lithuania, France and Denmark, while Ireland's approval had been withdrawn on 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: The amended deletion period for returning or deleting data is 60 days, and counting 60 days from 31 December 2026 gives 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller of a personal data breach without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of it. the notification must still describe the breach's nature, affected data, likely consequences and mitigation measures.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller of a personal data breach without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of it. The notification must still describe the breach's nature, affected data, likely consequences and mitigation measures.
justifications: The amendment replaced the notification deadline with 24 hours, while the notification content requirements remained unchanged.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: The breach was confirmed to expose usable privileged credentials, which triggers the 12-hour expedited outer limit rather than the standard 24-hour limit. Later confirmation of the credential exposure does not restart the clock.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Awareness was at 17:10 on 9 April, so the 12-hour expedited outer limit expired at 05:10 on 10 April. The first notice was delivered at 06:00 on 10 April, 50 minutes later.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: Counting from awareness on Friday 9 April, Monday 12 April is a closure and 14 April is the only approved pause, so the third counted Business Day is 16 April. The refused 16 April pause does not suspend that day.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: Records 001-050 are covered by two holds that are the same records, so release occurs when the later hold ends on 25 August 2027. The deadline is the later of the 60-day ordinary deletion date (29 August 2027) and the tenth Business Day after release (8 September 2027).

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: Backup BK-0630 was created on 30 June 2027 and contains no held records, so it must be deleted within 35 calendar days of creation. That period ends earlier than the 60-day ordinary deletion deadline, and a restore does not restart it.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: On 1 September 2027 the held ORD records are still retained solely under the legal hold and its deletion window, which permits only legal preservation. Service delivery and analytics uses are excluded, and the analytics request was rejected.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Approval begins no earlier than the latest of the proposed start date (20 April), the written Controller consent (18 April) and the completed security review (22 April). Actual processing in Stockholm also began on 22 April.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Added as an approved Sub-processor from 1 January 2027 for transactional email delivery and continuing ordinary transactional email from France. Meridian Mail Ltd is withdrawn and its emergency permission ends on 11 May 2027 and does not cover ordinary customer email.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: These countries have ongoing actual processing (Norway storage, Tallinn data centres, Vilnius monitoring, French email, Stockholm infrastructure) with effective authorisation still in place on 15 May 2027. Denmark, Ireland, and Finland are excluded because their authorisation was withdrawn, expired, or never granted, and Germany has no authorised processing.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: The security cap is the greater of EUR 2,000,000 and twice Qualifying Fees. Qualifying Fees of EUR 1,140,000 (VAT-excluded recurring fees of EUR 1,200,000 less the EUR 60,000 credit) give twice that amount of EUR 2,280,000, which exceeds the floor.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary cap is EUR 1,000,000 per Contract Year, and the EUR 300,000 earlier ordinary payment in the current Contract Year consumes part of it. Confidentiality and security payments do not consume the ordinary pool, leaving EUR 700,000.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: Ordinary claim L-1 is limited to the EUR 700,000 remaining ordinary pool. Security loss L-2 (EUR 1,750,000) fits within the remaining security pool of EUR 1,780,000, and the confidentiality losses L-3 and L-4 (EUR 250,000 and EUR 100,000) are uncapped and take precedence for the shared loss. The total payable is EUR 2,800,000.
